title: Turning threat-intelligence expertise into a field playbook
scope: Sales-led GTM contribution: threat-intelligence positioning, playbooks and field enablement.
collaboration: Rapid7's portfolio team and sales teammates, with field feedback shared across product and marketing.
decision: Turn product and buyer context into guidance a seller can use in a conversation, keeping supported findings separate from assumptions.
context: Selling a technical security product means explaining who it helps, which problem matters and why a buyer should act. That context also needs to be useful to other sellers.
contribution: At Rapid7, I wrote threat-intelligence playbooks the portfolio team used and served as a field resource for that motion. My competitive work also included briefs and source-backed positioning shared with teammates.
execution: I organized product and competitive context into field playbooks and briefs. I separated confirmed observations from assumptions so teammates had a clearer basis for positioning and discovery.
evidence: The public career timeline records the portfolio team's use of my Rapid7 threat-intelligence playbooks. The competitive-intelligence case study explains the field approach; employer documents remain private.
takeaway: A practical GTM contribution gives the next seller a clearer starting point. Playbooks should help people ask better questions and explain the product without overstating what the evidence supports.
reviewer: Pending Kristen Aing review of enterprise sales, GTM ownership and leadership copy
